claims.statement: The EU Data Act enables users of connected products to access raw or preprocessed use data and share it with a third party of their choice, subject to stated limits.

contrary_evidence: The Data Act source says inferred or derived data may be out of scope and obtained data cannot be used to develop a competing connected product.
A statutory access right does not guarantee clean APIs or permission for every proposed benchmark use.

economics.acquisition_route: Family installer pilot, revenue-sharing installation partners, equipment owners, then insurers and financiers
economics.founder_net_worth_path: A possible path is 50 enterprise customers at roughly 100000 PLN recurring revenue with high gross margin and founder-retained data-platform equity
economics.founder_time: Initially 12-18 hours per week with security and connector work partly contracted
economics.gross_margin_basis: Expected 70-85% after cloud, connectors, contributor rewards, security, and analyst support
economics.payback: Unvalidated; three to six enterprise licences could cover a lean first-year data platform
economics.pricing: Unvalidated: 40000-200000 PLN annual enterprise licence plus scoped studies; free or low-cost monitoring for contributors
economics.retention_or_repeat: Annual enterprise licences improve as cohorts lengthen; owner permissions require transparent renewal and revocation handling

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Longitudinal, multi-brand, permissioned data and contributor density create a dataset unavailable from a single vendor
fingerprint.customer: Energy-equipment financiers, insurers, manufacturers, distributors, and O&M providers lacking independent field benchmarks
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Installers embed permission in an optional monitoring service and receive a revenue share; enterprise customers are sold reports and APIs
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Owner-authorized telemetry ingestion, anonymized cohort benchmarks, failure-rate studies, and asset-owner diagnostics funded by enterprise licences
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: An enterprise pays an annual benchmark subscription or a scoped dataset and analysis licence
fingerprint.problem_trigger: A buyer must price performance or failure risk but has only vendor-specific or sparse operational evidence

founder_fit: Directly uses data science and AI skills
Leverages renewable-installation access without funding hardware ownership
Builds a scalable data asset rather than a manual service
Can be piloted part-time on a narrow equipment class
risks: Cybersecurity failure could harm equipment owners
Data licences may conflict with vendor terms, trade secrets, or personal-data rules
Biased cohorts could produce misleading benchmarks
Enterprise buyers may demand audit-grade provenance before paying

structure.control_point: Purpose-limited owner permissions to access and aggregate multi-brand connected-product telemetry
structure.critical_dependency: The relevant raw or preprocessed data must be technically accessible, standardizable, and lawfully reusable

thesis: Contract with owners of heat pumps, batteries, inverters, and EV chargers for permission to collect and aggregate their machine data, then sell cross-brand reliability and performance benchmarks to financiers, insurers, manufacturers, and maintenance firms.
title: Owner-Licensed Energy Asset Telemetry Trust
uncertainties: Unknown which target devices fall within accessible Data Act scope
Unknown API quality and cost across vendors
Unknown owner opt-in rate and enterprise willingness to pay
No lawful data-use agreement has been tested
